subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord guild channel allowlists support glob-pattern keys such as `ws-*`, and what precedence should those patterns have relative to exact channel entries, disabled entries, thread-parent fallback, category inheritance, and the literal `*` entry?
rationale: Automation should not choose this because the new syntax changes a public Discord config surface and determines which guild messages can reach agents.

options.title: Approve narrow glob contract
options.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

options.title: Defer to category/access redesign
options.body: Keep this open but require maintainers to fold the dynamic-channel problem into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60582 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/69748 before implementation.

options.title: Reject new glob syntax
options.body: Keep the exact-entry plus literal `*` model and document that dynamic workstreams should use the broad wildcard or the category/access-control trackers instead.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow glob contract
recommendation.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the shared matcher and Discord allow-list surfaces affected by this authorization decision.
